minor.issue: `PostIn` Pydantic model does not include a `visibility` field, so the value sent by the client is silently discarded. As a result, /api/users/{uid}/entities cannot actually filter private posts — the filter only works because posts never get a visibility field written. If the UI ever begins sending private/draft posts, they will leak on the public profile. Fix: add `visibility: Optional[str] = 'public'` to PostIn and persist `doc['visibility'] = inp.visibility` in create_post (server.py ~L1189-1198).

rca_of_issue: Post visibility leak RCA: /api/posts (POST) uses `PostIn` Pydantic model that omits `visibility`. In create_post, the response doc is built by explicitly picking known fields (text, media_url, media_type) — extra fields in the request body are dropped. Consequently, no post ever has a `visibility` value in Mongo. The /users/{uid}/entities filter `{'$or': [{'visibility':'public'}, {'visibility': {'$exists': False}}]}` matches every post because the field never exists. Reproduction: POST /api/posts with body {"text":"x","visibility":"private"} then GET /api/users/{uid}/entities — the private post appears in `posts`. Fix: (1) add `visibility: Optional[str] = 'public'` to PostIn; (2) in create_post add `'visibility': inp.visibility` when building doc. Severity: low today (no UI writes private posts yet); high if private/draft feature ships.
